assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_MIZUKAWA_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (11,637 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of Mizukawa Kōsuke (水川コウスケ) confined to the Recovery days story 『Dog』 (spine item S11) in Asaura's Japanese prose, located by spine item and paragraph. It closes with 'What might make him wait', which states what might again set him acting and what might make him pause, and which tests are missing. The discovery row claims behavior, psychology, ethics, relationships and decision-making, and does not claim speech; the portrait quotes almost none of it. He has no television identity, and the portrait treats talk of an older tower as his own speculation (11.176-179). The Recovery days reading, the cross-source crosswalk and the readiness manifest the portrait links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them directly. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Recovery days, 『Dog』 only. His history belongs to him at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: twenty-two, taken in by Okada six years earlier after a fatal encounter and hidden for a time, odd jobs and the punishment at the gambling room, staying because Okada was good to him (11.2-15, 11.31-32, 11.46-66). Located present states, all on one night: the attempt to stop him and his request to be severed (11.12-45, 11.67-73); the remembered ramen invitation and the boss's correction about Okada's last words (11.74-83); the boss lets him go and he bows (11.84-143); the quiet night and the informant's warning (11.183-197); the attempt on Ijūin (11.204-223); the fight with Chisato and Takina (11.241-281); Ijūin's attack, Chisato's account of who hired them and the fragment 水川を… (11.348-406); alone with the blade, the inventory of Okada's lessons, the boss's arrival and the long wait before yes (11.407-425). The split falls at the yes: his conduct after agreeing to come home is outside the evidence.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives a located account of a man who leaves what he cannot understand and does the job in front of him (11.2-15), whose refuge, job and recognition are all Okada (11.31-32, 11.53-66), and who turns an incomplete report into an immediate job of his own making: a possible motive and a real loss are enough to act on (11.67-83). It predicts his mistakes: accepting harm to uninvolved people while preferring less harm (11.204-223), filling a missing answer with his own guess (11.241-281), reading others' interventions as self-preservation (11.84-143, 11.348-406). Not B: what decides the long wait and the yes is not rendered, the portrait says nothing after the yes shows a renunciation of violence or a future outside the organization, and it says he waits only after others intervened and left him time; whether he would wait again or act is open, which is insufficiency. Not D: a dedicated portrait states located triggers and names what might make him wait.

Background history (Okada's rescue six years earlier, the gambling-room reputation, staying out of gratitude, 11.2-15, 11.31-32, 11.46-66) and one located change on a single night: from resolving to avenge with or without a command (11.74-83) to asking what he should do and saying yes after a long wait (11.407-425). Not C: one night, the change is a pause rather than a located new state, and the endpoint after the yes is withheld. Not E: background and a within-night change are located.

The row does not claim speech and the portrait does not analyze it. Located only as reported acts and fragments: polite address and an apology to the old boss and the request to be severed (11.12-45), thanks to the boss (11.84-143), asking his contact whether he has been sold out (11.183-197), repeating his opponents' names (11.241-281), repeating the object marker in 水川を… with surprise and objecting that the explanation is all self-preservation (11.348-406), and the yes (11.407-425). Not D: no register or forms are analyzed.

Located only: cheap student-style glasses, a tall stooped frame (11.2-15), odd jobs at the gambling room (11.46-52), the remembered invitation to eat ramen after Okada got back (11.74-83), bowing to seniors as Okada taught him (11.84-143). Not D: no routine or ordinary day is described.

Directed differences: Okada (care through concrete acts, trying to please him, the refuge, 11.31-32, 11.53-66); the old boss (politeness, apology, thanks, suspicion of fear or self-preservation, readiness to kill him if he must, a bow, then the long wait and yes, 11.12-45, 11.84-143, 11.407-425); the organization's members (overpowers them while recognizing they mean to protect him, 11.12-45); the informant (infers a warning under pressure and is grateful, 11.183-197); Chisato and Takina (repeats their names as Okada taught him, misreads whom they guard, 11.241-281, 11.383-391); Ijūin (single aim, 11.204-223, 11.348-406). Not B: the decisive relationship is with a dead man, and the living one with the boss lacks its outcome after the yes. Not D: directed differences are located.

The story is told close to him: why he is called a dog (11.2-15), his explanations for being spared and his lean toward fear or self-preservation (11.84-143), the inference about the informant (11.183-197), contemplating killing people who resemble his target (11.204-223), finding death the same way as Okada appealing (11.348-406), and the inventory of what Okada taught him (11.407-425). Not B: the long wait before yes, the decisive interval, is not given its reasoning. Not D: private reasoning is located at most turns.

Located conflicts on one night: overpowering the members sent to stop him (11.12-45); the confrontation with the boss in which he considers killing him and bows on leaving (11.84-143); the attempt on Ijūin with a woman beside him (11.204-223); the fight in which Chisato incapacitates him (11.241-281, 11.348-406); objecting to Chisato's account (11.348-406). Not B: one night, and whether he would again resort to violence after the yes is open. Not D: several distinct conflicts are located.

The row claims ethics. Located weighing: Ijūin's willingness to introduce a weapon read as possible lethal intent and the loss itself counted as enough (11.67-73); preferring no massacre of the uninvolved while having contemplated killing lookalikes and attacking with a bystander present (11.204-223); observing the form of respect while ignoring an order (11.84-143); the inventory that Okada taught him to live as a person and never to kill (11.407-425). Not B: how that inventory decides his choice is not rendered, and the portrait finds no test of responsibility for what the boss did to Ijūin. Not D: actual weighing is located.

The portrait covers his one story with spine-and-paragraph locators and keeps others' readings attributed: the boss's memory of Okada's watchdog remark, the boss's account of the death, Chisato's belief about Okada's wishes, the informant's part. Not B: speech is not analyzed, the source is one story, and the closing section is extrapolation without new locators. Not D: his whole appearance is covered with locators.

Located bounds against overreading: no order to punish the cheating customer is given (11.46-52); his gratitude is not shown to be false (11.74-83); the bound informant corroborates only part of his inference and does not show he understood the plan (11.247-254); Chisato admits nobody can know what Okada intended, and Okada's last sentence is never recovered (11.348-406, 11.407-425); the yes supplies neither a renunciation of violence nor a future outside the organization (11.407-425); the older tower is his speculation and establishes no television identity or institutional link (11.176-179). Not A: no forecast is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

His age (twenty-two) and the six-year interval since Okada took him in are given, and the one night is ordered by paragraph from the attempt to stop him to the yes. Not B: no calendar dates and one night. Not D: the order within the story is located.

scenario_readiness.note: The row does not claim speech and the portrait analyzes no register; only reported acts and one fragment are located.

conditions: An incomplete report that harm came to Okada, before the yes: predict that he makes it an immediate job of his own, counts a possible motive and a real loss as enough, and supplies the sanction himself with or without a command (11.67-83).

A report of harm to another person whose life mattered to him: the portrait itself names this transfer, but the evidence samples Okada only, so it is a separate, lower-confidence condition with the same prediction.

Members or seniors who block him in order to protect him: predict that he overpowers or evades them while recognizing their intent, addresses seniors politely, apologizes and observes the forms Okada taught him even while disobeying (11.12-45, 11.84-143).
Ambiguous help from a contact: predict that he infers a warning and is grateful without understanding the wider plan (11.183-197).

Include his mistakes: accepting harm to uninvolved people for a single aim while preferring less harm (11.204-223); filling a missing answer with his own guess (11.241-281); reading an intervention as self-preservation (11.84-143, 11.348-406).
A pause is predicted, with low confidence, only when others have intervened and left him time and the exact words are set beside a remembered ordinary lesson (closing section, 11.407-425).

Exclude his conduct after the yes, his life back in the organization, any exchange with a living Okada, any rejection of the boss or responsibility for the boss's act, any renunciation of violence, and anything that needs his speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The night of the revenge attempt in 『Dog』, with his six years under Okada as background, split at the yes: conditions apply before it, and nothing is predicted after he agrees to come home.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: The old boss as a senior he disobeys; organization members who try to stop him; an informant; Chisato and Takina as opponents whose assignment he misreads; Ijūin as target. Okada appears only in memory. A comparable new benefactor is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: The Kinshichō organization, its gambling room and the night's locations in Recovery days.
No television identity, no institutional link from the tower rumor, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation from the closing section and the located acts it rests on. The disposition that would decide his conduct after the yes is open and is excluded.
Ordinary social life is located only as odd jobs and a remembered meal invitation (11.46-52, 11.74-83).

conditions: Before the yes, a choice between acting on a single aim and sparing others: predict that he prefers less harm yet accepts risk to uninvolved people, and counts a possible intent and a real loss as reason enough (11.67-73, 11.204-223).
Excluded: any choice after the yes, and any claim that Chisato's assurance or his inventory of Okada's lessons changed his conduct.
scenario_readiness.note: One night of located weighing supports a narrow prediction before the yes; how his remembered lessons decide a later choice is not rendered.
The portrait establishes nothing about romance; absence is not evidence either way.
His organization work is located only as odd jobs and one unordered punishment whose effect on profits he hardly follows (11.46-52).

known_limits.statement: The story ends with his yes after a long wait; it supplies neither a renunciation of violence nor a future outside the organization, and his later conduct is unknown (11.407-425).
He pauses only after others intervened and left him time to himself; the portrait finds no test in which he waits unaided (closing section, 11.407-425).
Okada's intended last sentence is never recovered, and Chisato's assurance about his wishes is her belief, not a report (11.74-83, 11.348-406).
His stated preference for less harm sits beside contemplating killing lookalikes and attacking with a woman beside his target; neither alone describes him (11.204-223).
The older tower is his speculation; no television identity, institutional link or common timeline is established (11.176-179).
His speech is not analyzed in the portrait and not claimed on the row, so no register or voice can be modeled.
Untested: questioning a living Okada, an unequivocal rejection of the boss, taking responsibility for what the boss did to Ijūin, and being consulted again after he returns home.
